title: Majestic Opposition
reviewNotes: Three branches, 38 exact positions from the complete four-piece root. Saves the draw with Ka2, correcting captioned Ka1 (illegal from b3). The source ...Kc4 b5 ...Kxb5 Kb3 opposition line reaches a drawn pawn blockade. An independent direct promotion race draws, while the source Ka3 race loses to ...Qa1+/...Qb1+ and the queen skewer. Practice goal is draw.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players will lose trying. But only a true genius would be able to draw this position with white. You see, both pawns have the same distance from their respective promotion square. But the issue is that the white king is stopping his own pawn and the black king is shouldering our king. White is simply too slow to run and stop the pawn. Black is [music] going to get a queen and easily win. and going for example to A3 to make space for the pawn is not going to work despite both parts getting a queen. Now black plays queen to a1 check and after the king moves there is this skewer picking up the queen and winning the game for black and exactly the same thing happens after a king to a4 meaning that the brilliant only move and very counterintuitive move that draws this game for white is king to a1 stepping away from the entire action on the rest of the board but for a very specific reason. First of all, if the pawns now promote, there is going to be no skewer and this is simply a draw. But more importantly, after the pawn runs and we start running our own pawn, if black now tries to stop it, white is going to sacrifice the pawn with B5, black takes it. And now king to B3 not only gains opposition with the black king, but steps into the square of promotion of the black pawn. Meaning that if the pawn runs, the white king is now going to be able to stop it. And if the king goes to help the pawn, now we maintain a position. And this is simply a theoretically drawn endame.
